caption: The drawing depicts a detailed graphite illustration of a lidded tankard placed centrally on the paper. The tankard has a cylindrical body with a slightly flared bottom and a round base. It features a large, ornate handle on the left side, attached near the top and bottom of the vessel. The handle is decorated with a scroll motif and other intricate designs, and at the top, it connects to a hinged, domed lid with ribbed accents. The lid sits atop a wide, slightly projecting rim. The entire object is shaded to depict a metallic or reflective surface, suggesting a material like pewter or silver. In the lower left corner of the sheet, there is a smaller and simpler line drawing labeled "SIDE ELEVATION," showing the tankard in profile and emphasizing the handle's curve and the general shape. In the upper right corner of the drawing, there are handwritten notes: “MARK DEE YORK.” The border of the composition is marked with a drawn rectangular frame, and at the bottom right corner is a signature that reads "G.P. SANBORN." The drawing is monochromatic, rendered in shades of gray, and is displayed on a beige background.
title: Silver Tankard
